appearance_facts.fact: The chart title is 'Increasing Clean Grid Output from 2018 to 2023'.

appearance_facts.location: left side of the chart area
appearance_facts.fact: The vertical axis is labeled 'Grid Output (GWh)' with tick marks at 0, 400, 800, 1,200, 1,600, 2,000, 2,400, and 2,800.
The horizontal axis is labeled 'Year' with tick marks for 2018, 2019, 2020, 2021, 2022, and 2023.
A single blue line traces the data from left to right across the chart.
The line begins at the year 2018, at a value of 2,800 GWh on the vertical axis.
The line dips from 2018 to 2019, reaching a low point of 2,400 GWh.
The line rises to a peak in 2020, reaching a value higher than 2,800 GWh, approximately 2,850 GWh.
The line declines slightly from 2020 to 2021, then remains relatively flat from 2021 to 2023, ending at a value just below 2,800 GWh.

public_definitions: The dashboard trend is the overall direction of the clean-grid output line from 2018 to 2023.
The 'clean-grid output handling route' is selected based on this trend.
The three options are: 'routine clean-grid output monitoring', 'clean-grid output expansion follow-up', and 'clean-grid output decline response review'.
uncertain: The exact value at the peak in 2020 is not explicitly labeled, only visually estimated to be around 2,850 GWh.
